newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Next S.Africa fx control moves to help individuals.
newsitem.headline: Next S.Africa fx control moves to help individuals.

text.p: Individual South Africans are likely to benefit from further moves to gradually phase out exchange controls, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told reporters on Tuesday.
Stals said the time had come to broaden out exchange control relaxation beyond institutions and corporates.
"I am keen to get a decision from the (Finance) Minister and the Cabinet to do something for the private individual to enable him to make an investment outside of the country," Stals said.
"That will give us a measure of the demand there will be to take money out of the country from the private individuals," he said.
Individual South African investors can currently invest in funds with some exposure to international markets, but cannot make direct investments themselves.

Stals added the central bank would also be advising the Ministry of Finance to provide non-resident bonds redeemable over a number of years specifically tailored for South African emigrants who had over 10 billion rand in blocked funds left in the country.

"What we are advising the government is to provide a bond that will become repayable and fully convertible after some years. We will make this available to former residents who will be able to invest at least part of their blocked funds in these bonds," he said.

Stals said the central bank would hold serious discussions with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel over the next two or three weeks to discuss moves on relaxing exchange controls, which he reiterated would not be a "big bang" abolition.
The timing of any announcements would be up to Manuel, Stals said.
"Exactly when the Minister will take the decision, whether he wants to do it within the budget, or after the budget, I don't know," he said.
"Individuals will be the new part of it -- for the others you can only think of extensions when you talk about corporates and institutional investors," he said.
Manuel presents his budget on March 12.
